correctness.rationale: For a finite poset, comparable queried cells cannot be shattered. For an antichain, the all-in and all-out labels impose the two closure-size bounds; for any labelling the forced down-closure lies in the complement of the forbidden up-closure, and a linear extension of the difference realizes the desired intermediate size. On the square grid the two closures intersect exactly in the s queried points. Their total size must be at most m², so there are at least s cells incomparable to the entire support. Such cells occur only in the (m−s) unused rows and (m−s) unused columns, giving s≤(m−s)² and the stated ceiling. For the anti-diagonal prefix of length d_m, the down- and up-closures separately sum to d_m(2m−d_m+1)/2; the quadratic inequality makes the band nonempty and includes floor(m²/2). The argument includes s=0 and m=1 and does not say the displayed band is exhaustive. An independently written direct trace enumeration for every rank through m=4 gave central dimensions 0,1,1,2 (for m=4 the maximal band is actually k=5,…,11, wider than guaranteed). The source package's verify.py and verify_output.txt give an additional finite antichain-trace check, inspected without executing it; the all-order conclusion rests on the proof.

value.rationale: Middle fixed-area Ferrers layers are natural slices of a classical distributive lattice. Their trace complexity need not be read off from rank size or width. The quantitative square-root deficit supplies an exact all-order comparison with unrestricted width, and a concrete support gives every labelling on a specified interval of ranks. The claim does not determine the VC dimension at every rank.
